topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, audience, core themes, and specific learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Biological basis and experimental modeling of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as an accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations disrupting tissue differentiation and architecture, along with the laboratory models used to study it.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and the transition from benign to malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from benign precursor states to invasive and metastatic malignancies across clinical and histological contexts.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification rules
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and exceptions used to name benign and malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physiological and anatomical mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause patient illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across humans and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare tumor incidence and organ distribution across human populations, companion animals, and multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Approaches and challenges in cancer screening and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the principles, clinical efficacy, and limitations of early screening methods across various tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by reviewing the learning outcomes and providing housekeeping reminders for upcoming practicals.
